applicable_failures: The first scan wrote 2613 lines and about 695K characters of snippets, including 1001-00004 merger-agreement hits, and the broad path regex (agreement|contract|court|settlement) pulled in non-litigation matters. That output was too large and noisy.

The scan covered 1325 files but the path filter was restrictive: DOCX only, filenames matching a keyword list. Matters whose files are named differently would be dropped silently, and the agent never reported how many matters were in the full store.

The agent hand-picked 14 'strong' matters and the 1032-00002 exception from a second regex filter (prevailing party, enforce, award near attorneys). That filter can drop matters worded differently, e.g. cost-shifting or 'reasonable expenses' wording. The 57-matter hit list was reduced without showing what was excluded.

The first filter script failed with a heredoc syntax error and was rerun. The summary's selections rest on snippets only; no document was opened. 1005-00004 appears in the filtered output with an answer/defenses snippet that is not a fee clause.
critique.concerns: The scan completed and gave a candidate set, but the self-assessment overstates it. Candidates were chosen from regex snippets alone, with no document opened. The path restriction and the second narrowing regex may have dropped qualifying matters. Several listed matters (1005-00005, 1006-00004, etc.) have not been opened. Classification of 'strong' versus incidental was not verified.
critique.recommendation: Keep the full 57-matter hit list as the candidate set rather than the hand-picked 14. Open the specific documents with the snippets for each one and confirm that the clause actually shifts fees. Also check matters with hits outside the path filter by running a capped per-matter scan, printing 1-2 short snippets per matter.

Common failures at this stage in past runs:
- An uncapped store-wide scan with broad or common terms printed snippets for every match, producing millions of characters that filled the context before any response was written.
- A store-wide scan timed out or printed nothing after reaching only part of the store, and the agent accepted the partial output instead of narrowing by matter range or folder, rerunning, or searching file names, so qualifying matters never entered the candidate set.
- A scan had already surfaced every needed matter, but a follow-up filter on file names, folder names, exact phrases, or a hand-picked list silently dropped matters whose documents were named or worded differently.
- Matters were listed in file-name searches or scan output, but later scripts restricted to certain names or folders so the needed matter was never opened or examined.
What successful runs did: Passing runs also hit timeouts, but their output stayed bounded enough to read, and they often split the scan into parallel matter-range scripts or narrowed to a key acronym or per-matter hit counts, then picked candidates from what was reached.
Reconsider before moving on. If the goal was not fully reached, or any failure above applies, reopen this stage now: call stage_start with stage="Scan document text with an extraction script" and a goal that says what you will fix. Otherwise call stage_start for the next stage you need.
